thread.title: Cisco Gets A Buy Rating As Tax Law, Strategy Seen As Pluses | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD

author: Investor'S Business Daily
title: Cisco Gets A Buy Rating As Tax Law, Strategy Seen As Pluses | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD
text:
Reprints 
Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) will get a boost from the new corporate tax law as its growth strategy also picks up momentum, says Goldman Sachs, whose new computing analyst initiated coverage of the networking giant with a buy rating. 
Rod Hall, the Goldman Sachs analyst, set a price target of 48 on Cisco stock. Shares in Cisco edged down a fraction to 40.15 in early trading on the stock market today . 
"We see 2018 as a turning point for Cisco as the company moves to grow both revenue and gross profits as the transition to a disaggregated hardware/software model in campus switching gets underway," said Hall, formerly an analyst at JPMorgan. 
Cisco has stepped up acquisitions to speed up its shift to software and services from its core business of selling network switches and routers. 
A new corporate tax law enables U.S. companies to bring back cash from overseas at a lower rate. Cisco had about $70 billion in cash overseas as of Oct. 31. 
"Cisco is one of the top 3 beneficiaries of potential overseas cash repatriation (behind Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ))," added Hall. "We expect management to prioritize share repurchases and M&A with the repatriated cash." IBD'S TAKE: Finding the best stocks to buy can be tricky. That's why Investor's Business Daily makes it easy with educational tools , stock lists , research , Leaderboard and more. 
Cisco reports fiscal second-quarter earnings on Feb. 14. Cisco has forecast revenue growth in the December quarter amid strong demand for a new line of switches. Cisco's sales have dropped for seven consecutive quarters. 
"We see modest upside to consensus revenue expectations, but significant upside to the bottom line, mainly driven by our model incorporating the tax law changes," Hall added. 
Cisco stock had reached a 17-year-high before the market turned volatile last week, sending big-cap tech stocks down. Shares are trading near its 50-day moving average.
